title: Trace code and credentials across Jenkins boundaries
description: Switch scenarios to see where repository-controlled code executes, which path reaches deployment authority, and how the built-in node changes the controller's exposure. Select any component to inspect its responsibility.

nodes.label: Source repository
nodes.detail: Stores application code and the Jenkinsfile. Pull-request authors may also change tests, build scripts, and dependencies that the pipeline executes.

nodes.label: Jenkins controller
nodes.detail: Authenticates users, evaluates pipeline state, schedules work, stores configuration, and coordinates agents. It should not be a general-purpose build host.

nodes.label: Built-in node
nodes.detail: An execution context inside the controller process environment. A build here shares controller filesystem access and can interfere with the control plane.

nodes.label: Validation agent
nodes.detail: Runs repository-controlled compilation and tests with no production credential. A fresh agent or workspace reduces cross-build residue.

nodes.label: Artifact repository
nodes.detail: Stores the verified package or image under an immutable version and digest so later environments promote the same bytes.

nodes.label: Deployment agent
nodes.detail: Runs only reviewed promotion work, retrieves a verified artifact, and receives narrowly scoped deployment authority for the target environment.

nodes.label: Credential binding
nodes.detail: Makes a credential available only to the protected promotion step. Log masking reduces accidents but cannot stop trusted pipeline code from using the secret.

nodes.label: Production target
nodes.detail: Accepts the promoted artifact through an authenticated, auditable deployment operation. Jenkins does not make that operation idempotent automatically.

scenarios.label: Pull request
scenarios.summary: Repository-controlled code is scheduled onto an isolated validation agent with no production credential path.
scenarios.result: A faulty or malicious test can damage its worker, but the selected path keeps it away from the controller host and deployment authority.

scenarios.label: Built-in node
scenarios.summary: The same repository-controlled build runs on the controller's built-in node instead of an agent.
scenarios.result: The build shares controller filesystem access and resource pressure. Set built-in-node executors to zero and provide agents before moving production workloads.

scenarios.label: Protected promotion
scenarios.summary: A reviewed stage retrieves the verified artifact and receives a narrowly scoped credential on a separate deployment agent.
scenarios.result: The path separates untrusted validation from deployment authority and promotes the same verified bytes. The target operation still needs authorization, audit, and idempotent recovery.
